items.title: Solving Systems Containing Absolute Value Equations

sections.normalized_html:
[MATH: {y = 13; y =|− 3x + 4|]

The graphs of the given equations in the [MATH: xy]-plane intersect at the point [MATH: (x, y).] What are the possible values of [MATH: x?]
sections.readable_text:
[MATH: {y = 13; y =|− 3x + 4|]

The graphs of the given equations in the [MATH: xy]-plane intersect at the point [MATH: (x, y).] What are the possible values of [MATH: x?]

sections.normalized_html:
We are given the following system:

[MATH: {y = 13; y =|− 3x + 4|]

From the first equation, we know that [MATH: y = 13.]

Substituting [MATH: y = 13] into the second equation gives

[MATH: |-3x + 4| = 13.]

This absolute value equation has two cases:

  • If [MATH: -3x + 4 > 0,] we have [MATH: − 3x + 4|= 13; − 3x|= 9; x|= − 3.]

  • If [MATH: -3x + 4 < 0,] we have [MATH: − 3x + 4|= − 13; − 3x|= − 17; x|= (17)/(3).]

Therefore, [MATH: x = -3] and [MATH: x = \dfrac{17}{3}] are the two solutions of the given system of equations.
